newsitem.title: USA: NYSE April 21-25 program trading 14.7 pct volume.
newsitem.headline: NYSE April 21-25 program trading 14.7 pct volume.

text.p: New York Stock Exchange said Thursday that program trading for the week of April 21-25 averaged 14.7 percent of its average daily volume of 461.2 million shares, or 67.6 million shares,
Program trading accounted for an average of 13.9 percent of average daily volume of 477.0 million shares for the week of April 14-18.
Of the average 67.6 million shares traded during the week, buy programs accounted for an average 32.8 million shares, while sell programs accounted for an average 34.8 million.
In all markets, program trading averaged 84.5 million shares a day during the week of April 21-25.
The five member reporting the most program activity on the New York Stock Exchange were BNP Securities, Morgan Stanley, Saloman Bros, Natwest and Interactive Brokers
All five executed all or most of their program activity for customers, as agents or facilitator.

Program trading executed by firms as agent, for non-member customers, amounted to 67.8 percent during the week, while volume executed as principal, for their own accounts, amounted to 27.4 percent of program volume.
Program trading encompasses trading strategies involving the sale or purchase of a basket of at least 15 stocks with a total value of $1 million or more.
